✅ Major Active Volcanoes

1. Kīlauea (Hawaii, USA)– World’s most active volcano, continuous eruptions since 2024; shield volcano type.

2. Mount Etna (Sicily, Italy)– Europe’s most active volcano; frequent strombolian and effusive eruptions.
 
3. Stromboli (Aeolian Islands, Italy)– Called “Lighthouse of the Mediterranean”; continuous mild eruptions since 1934. 

4. Mauna Loa (Hawaii, USA)– Largest active volcano on Earth; shield type with massive lava flows.

5. Piton de la Fournaise (Réunion Island, France)– One of the world’s most frequently erupting volcanoes; effusive eruptions.

6. Merapi (Java, Indonesia)– One of Asia’s most dangerous volcanoes; frequent explosive eruptions; near dense population.

7. Reventador (Ecuador)– Active since 2008; continuous small explosive eruptions typical of Andean belt.

8. Mount Erebus (Antarctica)– Southernmost active volcano; has a permanent lava lake.

9. Nyamuragira (DR Congo)– Africa’s most active volcano; major effusive lava eruptions in Great Rift Valley.

10. Mount Vesuvius (Italy)– Active but presently dormant; last major eruption in 1944, potential threat to Naples.

11. **Mount Rainier (Washington, USA)** – Active stratovolcano; considered hazardous due to glaciers and lahars.

12. **Semeru (Indonesia)** – Indonesia’s highest volcano; continuous plume activity since 2019.

13. **Taal (Philippines)** – Caldera-type volcano; phreatomagmatic eruptions; near Manila region.

14. **Aira (Sakurajima, Japan)** – Frequent explosive activity; near Kagoshima, part of Aira caldera system.

15. **Sheveluch (Kamchatka, Russia)** – One of Russia’s largest and most explosive volcanoes.

16. **Ulawun (Papua New Guinea)** – Pacific “Ring of Fire” volcano; erupted March 2025; highly risky zone.

17. **Sabancaya (Peru)** – Active 2025; frequent ash plumes in Andes region.

18. **Lewotolok (Indonesia)** – Active since 2023; frequent ash explosions; located in Lesser Sunda Islands.

19. **Yasur (Vanuatu)** – Constant activity for 800+ years; strombolian eruptions visible nightly.
